newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai new airport gets three billion yuan loan.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai new airport gets three billion yuan loan.

text.p: Shanghai's second international airport, slated to open east of the city in 1999, has been granted three billion yuan ($361 million) in loans by the State Development Bank, the Xinmin Evening News said on Tuesday.
The longest duration for the loans would be 13 years and proceeds would be used to construct the airport's first-stage project, the newspaper said.

The State Development Bank also signed a contract with Shanghai Pudong Development Bank under which the Shanghai bank would act as guarantor and agent for the loans, it said, but gave no further details.

The new airport, to be built next to the sea in the Pudong New Area 30 km (18.75 miles) from Shanghai's city centre, would have an annual handling capacity of 70 million passengers and five million tonnes of cargo, the official media has reported.

The first phase would cost around 12 billion yuan with a 4,000-metre (13,000-ft) runway and a terminal of 150,000 square metres (1.6 million sq ft) as well as 50,000 square metres (540,000 sq ft) of commercial buildings, the reports have said.
Shanghai's Hongqiao international airport is in the west of the city.
